turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: why do you think adding an odd number to an even number would result in an odd sum?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess I thought that since one number is odd and the other is even, the result would still be odd. But now I'm not sure if that’s right. So, if \(2n\) is even, does that mean when I add it to something else, it changes? Can you explain how that works?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: what would happen if you tried your method on a simpler version of the problem?

turn_history.speaker: student

If I just add it to an odd number, like in my example, why does it not stay odd? Can you help me see why that happens?
